text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `runtime-prod` — metric `inference.latency.p95` > 2s (threshold 2000ms). Alert ID: PD#A12b3c. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/A12b3c

pagerduty: [automated] Incident A12b3c created and assigned to the on-call schedule.

alex: acked on PD. looking into it now. paging sounds like a p95 tail spike, not all traffic.

mike: tailing runtime logs — seeing a burst of retry loops from batcher at 1718004420-1718004500, a couple of GPU nodes hit OOM/restart? attaching recent pod events:
```
kubectl -n runtime-prod logs model-server-7f9 --since=2m
E OOMKilled: container killed
W Backoff 5m
```

kai: checking autoscaler metrics — there was a small scale-down at 1718003300 then a fast ramp up at 1718004400. Could be racing with cold starts. p50 is fine, p95 jumps during ramp.

sara: I see the same in tracing — KV cache miss rate spikes correlate with the p95. Probably cache warm-up + a few heavy long-context requests. Not seeing 500s in the API gateway.

oncall-bot: pagerduty update: incident A12b3c acknowledged by alex at 1718004550.

alex: I restarted the affected pod and bumped batcher concurrency down for the model shard. Observing metrics.

oncall-bot: pagerduty alert auto-resolved at 1718004629 (reason: threshold returned below alerting). Incident A12b3c now resolved automatically.

alex: it resolved automatically — but another page fired quickly after. this looks like flapping.

pagerduty: :rotating_light: New alert fired for service `runtime-prod` (same metric) — Alert ID: PD#A12b3d at 1718005122.

mike: I got the second page too. still seeing intermittent retries. looks like a noisy signal rather than steady outage.

kai: suggestion: increase the alert cooldown / add a min-firing-duration (e.g., 60s) to avoid transient spikes firing repeated pages. current rule is instant.

sara: agreed. 60s window + 2 evals would help. Also think we should add a mute for 10m while we stabilize to avoid wakeups.

jess: are any customers impacted? we need to triage the customer-impact bit before muting.

mike: checked SLO dashboard — no user-facing 5xx increase, but a handful of low-volume production keys saw latencies >5s for short windows. risk to realtime features but no broad outage.

alex: proposed actions: 1) mute alerts for 10m on PD (escalation disabled) 2) apply min-firing-duration 60s on the rule 3) open follow-up ticket to root cause (likely autoscale/coldstart + cache-warm).

sara: +1 to all. I'll create the follow-up and tag platform-team.

alex: mute command:
```
pd mute incident PD#A12b3d --duration 10m --reason "flapping transient, investigating"
```

oncall-bot: pagerduty note: alert PD#A12b3d muted by alex at 1718005300 for 10m.

kai: I'll draft a quick runbook reminder for next oncall: if you see two auto-resolves within 15m, consider muting and escalating to infra oncall rather than repeated ack cycles.

jess: thanks. for customer comms: we should say "no widespread customer impact, some latency spikes for specific workloads; monitoring and mitigation in progress" — ok?

mike: yep that's accurate.

alex: handing off to sara for the rest of window — i'm OOO in 20m. Sara is primary until 1718008199. leaving notes: scaled down concurrency, muted alert, follow-up ticket being created (PLAT-4567).

sara: taking over. I'll watch for further flaps and coordinate with infra if the mute ends and pages resume.

oncall-bot: handover recorded: alex -> sara at 1718005640.

pagerduty: alert mute expired for PD#A12b3d at 1718005900. No new alerts fired during mute.

alex: thanks team :thumbsup: filing retrospective note later.

sara: creating follow-up ticket now. contents: chronology, metric graphs, pod events, autoscaler timing, proposed alert tuning (60s window + 2 evals), and recommended runbook update.

sara: PLAT-4567 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-4567 — tagging infra and oncall.

mike: small ops note — add `min_p95_eval_count: 3` to the rule to reduce noise for models with bursty traffic.

kai: agree. after follow-up we should push the rule change during low traffic.

jess: good handoff. closing thread for now unless it flaps again. :white_check_mark:
